rating.reasoning_summary: This strand tracks the meta-discourse around defining and explaining 'TPOT' (This Part of Twitter) from 2022-2025. The boundary object is Christine's 2022 'Guide to TPOT'—a curatorial artifact attempting to make the subculture legible. Rather than evolving the concept itself, the strand shows a recurring pattern: newcomers ask 'What is TPOT?', insiders provide varying answers (sincere guides, ironic jokes, gatekeeping), and the definition remains fundamentally unstable. The discourse is constructive in intent (helping onboard) but reveals dialectical tension between legibility and exclusivity. The 'idea' doesn't evolve; instead, the *need to explain* persists as the community grows, with later tweets (2024-2025) showing fatigue and irony replacing the earnest curation of 2022.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Artifact: Christine's original 'Guide to TPOT' (2022)—the most earnest attempt at legibility and onboarding.
The Skeptical Turn: Spacepope argues TPOT isn't real, just 'a joke taken too far'—introducing definitional instability.
Utility Signal: Tyler uses Christine's guide as the default answer to 'What's TPOT?', validating its role as boundary object.
The Ironic Backlash: Nosilverv mocks the guides as 'really really bad'—signaling insider gatekeeping vs. newcomer legibility.
The Joke Definition: PrinceVogel claims TPOT = 'The Prince's Orbit of Twitter'—playful ego but also revealing the subjectivity of all definitions.
Visual Meme: Forthrighter's Sisyphus image (2024) captures the futility of defining TPOT—the question recurs eternally.
Infrastructure Signal: Discovery of a 'TPOT website' suggests attempted formalization beyond Twitter.
Exhaustion: Touchmoonflower's screenshot mocking TPOT's self-perception shows the discourse turning self-critical.
Conflict Node: Hahnbeelee's critique of TPOT misogyny/racism—revealing darker undercurrents beneath the 'vibes' discourse.
The Current State: Nosilverv's 2025 tweet shows TPOT now defined by shared practices (Jhanas, TRE) rather than ideas—a shift from ideology to ritual.
